summary: Harikanta Overseas: Hold — unresolved; high impairment risk. BQS / Growth Quality Score / IAS are NS. FY26 growth and low March debt are counterbalanced by weak cash conversion, unverified October IPO deployment, unresolved cash-flow classifications and incomplete primary liquidity. All ordinary return/entry fields are null; only explicitly funded conditional scenarios may show non-rescue returns, with bear rescue modeled separately.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Harikanta Overseas is a small, concentrated textile manufacturer/trader undergoing a production and capacity transition. It is not yet an evidence-backed compounder. FY26 group revenue reached ₹46.0814 crore, up 31.01%, and PAT ₹7.1362 crore, up 61.34%. Core operating EBITDA excluding other income was ₹10.4484 crore. The decisive concern is cash realization: FY26 receivables rose 244.86% to ₹13.7971 crore, absorbed ₹9.7963 crore of cash, and two-year group CFO/PAT was only 0.211×. March debt is low and a ₹24.297 crore gross IPO could materially improve capacity to fund expansion, but the actual October bank/deployment bridge is unavailable.

At the corroborated secondary ₹69 close on 19 October, market capitalization is ₹68.0736 crore and historical current-share P/E is 9.54×. Neither that multiple nor a mechanical post-IPO book value establishes an investable margin of safety. BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS), and IAS are all NS. Classification: Hold — unresolved; high impairment risk. The business has real operations and favorable reported growth, but attributable capital returns, comparable organic growth, current funding and executable liquidity need evidence before an ordinary return or entry can be stated. This is conditional analytical research, not a personalized recommendation or trading instruction. [S1–S4][M1–M3]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Thirteen factor audits are provided with supporting facts, contrary evidence, rationale and traceable citations. Scores are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV NS, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5; the price-sensitive factors are R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. Missing scores are not zero or a neutral five, and weights are never renormalized.

BQS has exactly 3.00 known contribution at 68% coverage; its raw mathematical missing-input bounds are 3.32–6.20. GQS has 2.05 known contribution at 45% coverage and raw bounds 2.60–7.55. CASH 3 triggers an explicit ceiling of 5 because weak operating cash conversion persists across both available group years, not because investing capex reduces CFO. The cap-adjusted bounds are 2.60–5.00, but GQS remains NS. The short history and possibility of temporary collection lag are important contrary evidence, not hidden certainty.

IAS uses final BQS once at 25%. Only D is scoreable directly, contributing 0.60 at 20% coverage. Direct missing-input bounds are 1.40–8.60; propagating the tighter BQS bounds gives 1.98–7.65. These are exact Decimal mathematical bounds, not probabilities, confidence intervals, targets or ranking points. All three aggregates remain ineligible for numerical ranking. A one-point change in MOAT and EXEC together shifts BQS bounds by 0.28 but cannot cure missing growth, capital or funding evidence. No severe-governance or actual-funding-failure numerical override is asserted without evidence. [E1–E20]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The group makes and trades woven synthetic and viscose fabrics for sarees, dress materials, kurtas and other garments, with a Surat manufacturing base. Its disclosed mix includes Ikat, polyester garment and saree fabrics, dhupion, poly linen and natural-fiber products. Fabric manufacturing, trading and subsidiary jobwork must be distinguished: identical FY25/FY26 parent and consolidated sales do not mean that the acquisition had no economic impact, because intragroup jobwork is eliminated while production profit and assets change perimeter.

FY26 disclosed revenue comprises ₹25.5633 crore local sales, ₹19.3509 crore export sales and ₹1.1673 crore export benefits, summing to ₹46.0815 crore with ₹0.0001 crore rounding versus the face statement. FY25 was ₹18.9641/15.5592/0.6499 crore. Export benefits are revenue here, whereas older accounts included such benefits in other income. FY25 Ikat product revenue was ₹25.3629 crore, about 73.47% of product sales excluding benefits; the November 2025 share was approximately 75.63%. The business is therefore not evenly diversified merely because a product list is long.

Orders generally arrive as purchase orders rather than long-term protected contracts. Cash must finance yarn, processing, inventory and customer credit. Wedding/festive and export demand can recur, but sales can fluctuate with fashion, yarn prices, customer inventory and competition. Profit is economically realized only after collection. Current product/customer profitability, direct customer retention, order-book cancellation terms and independent market share are ND. [S1][S2]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantages are production know-how, product consistency, turnaround time, customer relationships and Surat sourcing proximity. They are useful operating capabilities, not by themselves a durable moat. No independently demonstrated proprietary technology, enforceable exclusivity, enduring pricing power or market-share gains were established. FY25 top-customer concentration of 22.26%, top-five 66.54% and top-ten 78.62% increases bargaining and disruption risk. The eight-month November table shows top-ten 83.31%; this is not an authenticated October 2026 concentration. Supplier concentration improved materially: the top supplier fell from more than 80% in FY23–FY24 to 8.02% in FY25, an important counterpoint to a one-sided fragility narrative.

Three different comparisons illuminate economics without fabricating a peer valuation median. Betex India is a processing/dyeing/printing-jobwork comparator: FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹100.3385 crore and PAT ₹5.6902 crore, but an employee-benefit actuarial accounting qualification makes reported profitability an imperfect benchmark. Jobwork net revenue is also not equivalent to gross fabric sales. Swasti Vinayaka Synthetics appears in the prospectus with FY25 revenue ₹38.3806 crore, EPS ₹0.27 and ROE 10.54%; these are issuer-reproduced peer figures, not an independently retrieved peer report. Its March 2026 price/multiple is stale and not used as an October benchmark. Sangam India illustrates a broader integrated yarn, fabric and garment platform with five plants and export reach beyond 54 markets; FY25 product mix was more diversified. That is a stronger scale/diversification comparison, not a claim that its equity is a superior investment.

MOAT 4 reflects a contestable niche with real operating capabilities. The absence of analyst coverage or small size is not itself a penalty. No verified textile TAM or market share is inserted merely to make the runway look large. [S2][P1–P3]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The extracted FY20–FY26 revenue series is ₹7.7806932, ₹9.9703561, ₹7.1352532, ₹14.9027, ₹11.1122, ₹35.1730 and ₹46.0814 crore. Annual additions are ₹2.1897, −₹2.8351, ₹7.7674, −₹3.7905, ₹24.0608 and ₹10.9084 crore. The record contains contractions as well as rapid growth; the FY25 216.53% increase should not be extrapolated.

Reported endpoint three-year CAGR is 45.69% and five-year CAGR 35.82%. Ten-year CAGR is ND. These are clearly labeled descriptive mixed-history calculations, not scoreable organic growth. FY22 export benefits of ₹0.1774184 crore were in other income; original FY23/FY24 product sales of ₹14.3839186/10.5801512 crore differ from restated revenue ₹14.9027/11.1122 crore inclusive of benefits. Production machinery was transferred from promoter concerns in September 2024 and Harikanta Weaving acquired in November. The current perimeter thus represents more than a continuous same-asset growth history.

FY26 revenue grew 31.01% and operating EBITDA 55.64% on the selected statutory comparative. This is real disclosed growth but price, volume, utilization, product mix, acquired production and intercompany margins cannot be quantitatively separated. REV is consequently NS for sustainable comparable growth, not an allegation that audited sales are false. Needed evidence is at least a reconciled historical pro-forma operating perimeter, metres sold and realized price by category, customer additions/retention and mature-versus-new machinery profitability. [S1–S5]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The prospectus shows installed fabric capacity rising from 125,440 metres in FY23 to 204,288 in FY24 and 1,201,258.4 in FY25, with FY25 usage 1,112,032.6 metres. This reflects transferred machinery as well as organic operating development. The proposed expansion is 38 looms: 20 rapier, 10 airjet and eight high-speed rapier, together with a factory building on leased premises. Three proposed capacity rows sum to 3,318,919 metres and achievable rows to 2,914,260.48, but prose describes post-expansion capacity of 1,448,400. These definitions need reconciliation before estimating incremental revenue from capacity.

The final offer estimates ₹24.297 crore gross proceeds, ₹3.5111 crore issue expenses and ₹20.7859 crore net proceeds. Uses are ₹5.4035 crore factory, ₹9.325 crore machinery, ₹4.75 crore working capital and ₹1.3074 crore general corporate purposes. At the prospectus date orders had not been placed, quotes were time-limited, construction was expected over six to eight months and production targeted FY27. These statements are plans, not commissioned output. An undated lead-manager track record has conflicting price/date labels and zero actual utilization alongside an implementation-amount table; it cannot establish current unused cash or delivery.

Operating invested capital is ₹12.8166 crore in FY25 and ₹22.0692 crore in FY26. NOPAT at an analyst 25% tax rate gives average ROIC 39.25% and one-year incremental proxy 25.14%. The operating and financing reconciliations agree to ₹0.0001 crore rounding. Yet a blended one-year proxy does not attribute returns to the acquired subsidiary, transferred machines, incremental receivables or proposed looms. Three/five-year attributable incremental ROIC is ND; CAP remains NS. An attractive runway requires both demand absorption and funded collection discipline. Neither a large industry nor low March leverage proves high-return reinvestment. [S1][S2][S9]

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text:
Related-party dealings deserve a complete economic review. FY25 involved machinery purchases of roughly ₹2.04 crore from five promoter-linked concerns and acquisition of the weaving subsidiary from promoters for approximately ₹0.7536 crore. FY26 machinery advances include ₹0.2021 crore to Abhishek and ₹0.2800 crore to Tripura. Three directors received aggregate remuneration ₹0.5450 crore, with other related-family salaries separately disclosed. Treasury holdings of ₹2.4675 crore mutual funds plus ₹0.7219 crore PMS coexist with bank debt and a growing receivable balance. This is a capital-allocation question, not proof of diversion.

The FY27 AGM notice proposes related leases totaling ₹1.18 crore across four concerns. The company says these premises/machines are already in use, the arrangements preserve operational continuity, pricing is arm’s length and approved by the audit committee, and interested promoters would abstain. Those explanations are retained. A notice is not final shareholder approval; the underlying voting-result PDF could not be retrieved. Likewise, prospectus paragraphs give inconsistent descriptions of non-compete protection: one refers to agreements covering five entities, another says there are no formal restrictions for two proprietorships, while business text describes a 20-year arrangement. Enforceable scope and actual contracts remain unverified.

The FY26 audit and internal-control opinions are unmodified; the auditor reports no fraud or loan default. CARO nevertheless notes ₹0.3974 crore loans without scheduled repayment, making overdue-status assessment unavailable, and a delayed Kotak charge registration. CSR of ₹0.0516 crore was not spent during FY26, but the auditor says it was spent subsequently, so it is not presented as still unpaid at cutoff.

A.H. Jain resigned in August. The attributed reason is other professional commitments, with no disagreement over accounting/reporting, no integrity concern, no information denial and no pending review. The annual report confirms the resignation and proposal of Jain Shrimal as replacement. Final approval is not assumed. Separately, the mirrored board response says FY26 results were three days late during the first post-listing administrative transition; the ₹15,000 fine plus ₹2,700 GST was paid and compliance calendars/supervision strengthened. These are disclosed company explanations, not authenticated original BSE PDFs. G1 is Conditional, not a misconduct finding. [S1][S2][S10][S11]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The historical table, standalone/group reconciliation and annual cash bridges are embedded below and in the canonical record. FY26 group PBT ₹9.2928 crore becomes PAT ₹7.1362 crore after current tax, prior-period and deferred-tax effects. Other income of ₹0.6440 crore includes FX gain ₹0.3543 crore, interest subsidy ₹0.1681 crore, investment/interest/dividend and other items. Removing all other income and applying 25% tax produces a conservative normalized PAT proxy ₹6.4866 crore; this is not a claim that all FX or subsidy income is one-off. Operating EBIT is ₹9.1293 crore and EBITDA ₹10.4484 crore. A clean comparable gross margin is ND because yarn, trading, subcontracting and factory conversion costs are not adequately separable.

FY26 pre-working-capital operating cash ₹10.7873 crore is reduced mainly by ₹9.7963 crore receivables absorption, partly offset by ₹1.1023 crore inventory release and ₹1.9761 crore payables support. Cash generated before tax is ₹3.5702 crore; cash tax ₹0.8087 crore leaves CFO ₹2.7615 crore. Cash capex ₹1.8832 crore gives reported FCF ₹0.8783 crore; deduct financing-classified interest ₹0.4468 crore to obtain ₹0.4315 crore after capex and cash interest. The poor CFO conversion is not explained away as capex. FY25 group CFO was −₹0.3208 crore, making two-year CFO/PAT 0.211×; parent-only conversion is even lower at 0.116×. Do not splice earlier standalone cash flows into a three/five-year group ratio.

Receivables increased from ₹4.0008 crore to ₹13.7971 crore. Average FY26 receivable days are 70.49; closing days are 109.28 versus 41.52 in FY25. The company ages from bill date because its software cannot provide due-date aging, so ₹2.0379 crore older than six months is not automatically overdue. ₹0.7246 crore is over one year, all reportedly good. Inventory/payable-day proxies of 67.87/82.90 use incompatible cost bases, so no spurious precise cash-conversion cycle is stated. March bank balances ₹3.0138 crore contain ₹1.7993 crore restricted margin money, leaving only ₹1.2145 crore unrestricted. ₹0.4821 crore machinery advances are excluded from operating working capital and transferred once to PPE in models.

Two material reconciliations remain open. Statutory FY25 PAT ₹4.4231 crore differs from restated ₹4.4680 crore; the prospectus’s ₹4.23 lakh adjustment is labeled dividend income while adjoining explanation discusses gratuity/leave. Statutory CFO/CFI/CFF −0.3208/−7.2810/8.8817 differ from restated −0.4317/−7.1773/8.8889 but reconcile to the same cash change. The acquired ₹3.884 crore net-PPE line is not an extra cash acquisition price on top of the parent’s ₹0.7536 crore share purchase. November 2025 cash-flow rows visibly sum to −₹1.3027 crore investing cash, not the stated −₹0.4468 crore, because a repeated dividend row is inconsistent. The discrepancy is retained, not silently repaired or treated as an actual extra outflow.

Reported FY26 EPS ₹9.92 uses 7,195,740 weighted shares; current-share EPS is ₹7.2333 on 9,865,740 shares. IPO share growth is 37.11%, old-holder ownership dilution 27.06%. FY25 statutory EPS ₹9.58 and bonus-adjusted restated EPS ₹6.69 use different denominators. Bonus arithmetic is not economic dilution. Clean audit opinions and positive current operating earnings are meaningful counterevidence, but G2 remains Hold pending authoritative reconciliation. [S1–S5][M1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹69, equity capitalization is ₹68.0736 crore. FY26 current-share P/E is 9.54× and conservative normalized-proxy P/E 10.49×. March book P/B is 3.26×. Adding estimated net IPO proceeds mechanically to March equity gives ₹41.6953 crore and 1.63× P/B, but this is not an authenticated October balance sheet. A stale March cash/debt/treasury EV of ₹67.2862 crore implies 6.44× operating EBITDA; it deliberately does not pretend to include unknown post-IPO movements. Reported FCF yield is only 1.29%. A low headline P/E is therefore not an independently funded owner-cash yield.

Models begin with the 31 March 2026 reported balances, explicitly bridge to the 19 October entry, then forecast the remaining FY27 stub, FY28–FY31 and the March-to-October 2031 terminal stub. They do not grant a full five years of growth after an already advanced fiscal terminal date. Actual dated horizon is 1,826/365.25 years, essentially five calendar years. Terminal TTM uses 163/365 of FY31 plus 202/366 of FY32, not weights forced to sum to one; FY32 includes a leap day after exit. The pre-entry bridge is conditional, not a newly invented interim statement. Net IPO proceeds are entered once after estimated fees; ₹4.75 crore working-capital earmarking is not deducted again alongside modeled ONWC. Factory/machinery spending is modeled once, old capital advances transfer without new cash, debt principal is repaid explicitly, and legacy net tax/CSR/GCP are one-time pre-entry uses.

Base growth decelerates from 12%/15%/14%/12%/10% to 8%, EBITDA margin normalizes from 21% to 20%, and ONWC/revenue improves to 28%. Bull assumes stronger absorption; bear combines a 15% initial sales loss, margin compression, 25% project overrun and materially worse working capital. No new bank facility is invented to rescue negative cash. All ordinary IRRs and entry prices are null because October funding is unverified. Only the explicit counterfactual base and bull clear each required operating floor, producing conditional annual returns of 20.33% and 35.68%. Their 15%-hurdle mathematical prices ₹86.53/157.71 are not recommendations. Bear breaches the floor and its non-rescue return/entry remain null even though later cash improves.

The terminal bridge values operating EBITDA, retains 3%–4% revenue as operating cash, adds only excess cash and a haircut-adjusted investment portfolio once, and subtracts remaining debt/employee claims. It does not add property, IPO proceeds, prepaid capex, restricted deposits, warrants or legacy taxes again. DCF independently models FCFF, operating/restricted cash reinvestment and terminal growth divided by assumed incremental ROIC. WACC 14%–18%, terminal growth 3%/5% and terminal incremental returns 12%/18% are sensitivities, not measured CAP. A separate bear rescue at ₹48.30 per new share with 5% fees requires ₹7.2005 crore gross, creates approximately 1.4908 million shares and yields −12.55% annualized for the original shareholder. It is not an ordinary return.

The full 48-cell growth/margin/multiple grid, DCF grid, rescue-discount/fee, opening-cash, execution-cost and hurdle sensitivities are embedded. Holding other model assumptions fixed, constant growth required to meet 15% is about 12.29%/6.63%/2.48% at 6×/8×/10× exits; those mathematical solutions require no rescue in that particular grid but still depend on the unverified opening bridge. They are not objective market expectations. R and P remain NS. [S1][S2][S9][M1–M3]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Risk
sections.text:
The central stress is not merely a falling P/E. A large buyer reduces orders, fabric prices or mix weaken, new looms are late, debtor collection lengthens and working capital consumes IPO liquidity before capacity earns an adequate return. The bear case starts with a 15% sales decline, EBITDA margin 12% then 10%, ONWC/revenue near 48%, 5% maintenance spending, 25% project overrun and a 6× terminal EBITDA valuation. These are explicit analyst stresses, not reported events. Low debt at March does not eliminate the need to fund the operating cycle and contractual capex.

In this linked stress the first required cash-floor breach is 31 March 2027, with a peak unfunded gap ₹6.8404 crore. Negative balances are not disguised as an automatically available overdraft. Non-rescue conditional IRR and entry are null, even if terminal cash later recovers. The distinct equity rescue charges 5% on gross proceeds, issues at a 30% discount to the reference quote, and records cash and share changes at the periods where needed. Its roughly −12.55% annual return reflects permanent per-share loss; a later recovery in aggregate enterprise value need not restore an original holder’s economics.

Additional risks are customer concentration, related-party asset/lease pricing, old bill-age receivables, uncertain project capacity definitions, future compliance and exit queues. Book PPE, bank margin collateral and a factory on leased premises are not independent cash liquidation floors. No family-guaranteed property is counted as company equity. The investment portfolio is haircutted in stress and is not counted both as funding and terminal surplus. There is no verified default or established fraud, and real operations, low March debt and potential net IPO funds are important counterpoints. D 3 means credible permanent-loss risk warrants caution, not that failure is inevitable. [S1][S2][M1][M2]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold share-price gains over five years require 37.97% and 58.49% annualized appreciation, respectively. At unchanged current shares, a 10× terminal P/E and 12% net margin, the required revenues are approximately ₹283.64 crore for 5× and ₹567.28 crore for 10×, versus FY26 ₹46.08 crore. This is a scale identity, not a forecast or valuation target. Such outcomes need sustained demand, profitable capacity, credit discipline, cash funding and minority-friendly capital allocation. A higher exit multiple cannot replace these requirements.

The bull case terminal TTM revenue is only about ₹129.07 crore and its conditional per-share terminal price ₹317.18 is about 4.60× the reference price, still short of 5×. It assumes no adverse new equity issue because its conditional cash model stays funded; an actual funding shortfall could change that. The current share denominator already incorporates the IPO, so historical EPS cannot be multiplied by a target multiple without adjusting for issued shares. Rescue financing reduces original holders’ share of future equity.

A larger nominal textile market and inconsistent proposed capacity rows do not establish accessible profitable market share. With no comparable long-run organic revenue or attributable incremental-return record, the 5×/10× proposition is speculative and unsupported. Revisit only after actual commissioning, customer absorption, cash collections and return-on-new-capital evidence. [S1][S2][M1]

sections.title: Monitoring Triggers
sections.text:
Priority one is a dated consolidated funding pack: unrestricted bank balances separate from margin money, sanctioned and actually available facility limits, maturities/renewals, remaining project payments, utilization of IPO proceeds and commissioning certificates. A use-of-proceeds landing page or notice is not proof of funds or production. Resolve the capacity-table/prose inconsistency and determine whether ₹0.4821 crore old machinery advances overlap new-project invoices. The model conservatively keeps planned new spending separate and makes that uncertainty explicit.

Priority two is cash reliability: issuer/auditor reconciliation of the FY25 statutory/restated classifications, acquisition-date cash/debt/PPE and the November 2025 CFI subtotal. Obtain subsequent collection of the ₹2.0379 crore older-than-six-month bills, current customer concentration, debtor-credit terms and advances. An improvement in revenue accompanied by further receivables absorption would not resolve CASH. Observe two or more comparable post-expansion periods with positive cash after maintenance capex and interest; do not score success merely from a single invoice-heavy quarter.

Priority three is capital and governance: project-level operating profit, utilization and incremental capital; actual related-party terms and arm’s-length support; verified voting outcomes, auditor appointment and compliance updates. A non-adverse resignation explanation should remain on record while evidence develops. No presumption of an enforcement event is justified.

Before any implementation, authenticate primary BSE history, current lot and trading eligibility, surveillance flags, spread and available bid depth. The observed 60-session median close×volume is ₹350,400 and 20-session median ₹439,200, but these are partial secondary proxies. At 5% participation, a 1,200-share whole lot requires 24,000 shares daily volume; only nine of 53 observed sessions in the 60-session frame and three of 17 in the 20-session frame qualify. The 19 October 1,200-share day cannot accommodate one whole lot at 2%, 5% or 10% participation. Continuous-position proxies of about 28.36/22.62 days at 5% do not guarantee a six-lot exit. Missing dates stay unknown and L remains NS. [S1][S2][M1–M4]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification is Hold — unresolved, not a forced Buy/Sell judgment and not a claim of insolvency. BQS, Growth Quality Score and IAS are NS with the exact disclosed bounds and no numerical rank. G1 is Conditional; G2/G3/G4 are unresolved Holds. The useful next step is evidence completion, especially current funding, reconciled cash and attributable operating returns, rather than refining a false-precision target price.

An upgrade would require a coherent funding/deployment bridge with sufficient cash floor under realistic stress, collected working capital, verified expansion delivery, comparable profitable growth and defensible returns on the incremental capital. Deterioration would include credible evidence of unfinanceable commitments, persistent overdue collections, materially adverse related-party treatment or unreliable accounts that cannot be reconciled. These are conditional research triggers, not claims that such events occurred or instructions to transact.

Ordinary return and entry fields remain null across the full record. The base/bull conditional outcomes are illustrations only; the bear rescue is explicitly separate and dilutive. No dividend is counted while the same cash is retained at exit. No unsupported live price, broker access or portfolio suitability is assumed. Position sizing here is solely the framework’s ₹5 lakh lot-aware execution test. [S1][S2][M1–M4]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source register distinguishes actual primary documents read, primary security metadata, issuer-reproduced peer data, secondary price histories, secondary company-response mirrors and inaccessible primary pointers. Company annual reports and the final prospectus are actual retrieved PDFs; raw originals, extracted/OCR text and page images are excluded from the portable analytical package. Safe financial extracts retain original URLs, SHA256 digests, scope, units and locators. Reproduction of calculations does not freshly authenticate external source content.

BSE resignation, SOP response, voting, AGM and CIN PDFs returned inaccessible responses. Those responses are not original documents and no successful PDF hash is claimed. A secondary mirror preserves the company’s delay explanation and a secondary report preserves the auditor’s non-adverse reasons; neither is labeled exchange-authenticated. The AGM notice is evidence of a proposal only. The undated lead-manager tracking sheet is not assumed to have been available by cutoff or to establish current funding; it is retained solely as a conflicting contextual record. Betex and Sangam annual reports were read; Swasti figures are only the issuer’s reproduced comparison. Original older scanned reports have uneven OCR quality, so selected FY25 figures use the readable FY26 comparative and older unlocatable cash flows stay null.

Forecasts assume no dividends, no bank rescue, explicit debt repayment, conservative current-share economics and stated tax, margin, working-capital, capex, cash-floor and exit sensitivities. Actual October bank balances, full interim statements, complete primary trading history, project returns, current customer concentration, machinery commissioning and legal enforceability of related arrangements remain ND. NS means not scoreable, not zero. Analysis stops at conditional research where material evidence is missing. This is not personalized financial advice; verify fresh filings and executable terms before making an investment decision. [S1–S11][P1–P3][M1–M4]
